Final categorization: POSSIBLE  
(Justification: This is a non-review research paper that estimates future monetary values of ecosystem services under four global land-use scenarios (Market Forces, Fortress World, Policy Reform, Great Transition) to 2050. The study uses projected land-use changes from the Great Transition Initiative (GTI) as input—including urban, cropland, forest, grassland, desert—and adjusts these for biomes like wetlands and coral reefs not covered by GTI. It produces global and national-scale maps of ecosystem service values at 1 km² resolution and reports country-level results for all nations in supplementary materials. However, LULC prediction is not the primary objective; rather, it is an input to value ecosystem services monetarily. The paper does not develop or validate its own LULC model, nor does it report quantitative accuracy metrics (e.g., validation statistics, error rates) for the land-cover projections—it adopts and slightly adjusts pre-existing GTI land-use projections. Thus, while it includes national-scale spatial implementation and multiple future scenarios, LULC prediction is used instrumentally, not as the central research focus.)
